{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABZleqhA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhDMAlE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 47, "title": "Preserve PMX bone morphs and mixed vertex/bone groups through glTF, VMD/VPD and Demo", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `631a5946744180e15d3704d43244656d1d9c0ded`, `tools/pmx-morph.ts` emits executable targets only for vertex morphs and vertex-only groups. Bone offsets are discarded. `bindMorphMotion()` rejects identities with `target:null`, and reusable controls and Demo sliders expose geometry-target vectors only.

Consequently, VMD cannot animate bone morphs, groups containing bone children cannot execute, and manual morph application cannot contribute to the existing IK/append/physics pipeline.

## Expected outcome

Deliver one complete bone-morph feature across extension definitions, converter, reusable Three.js APIs and Demo. Support PMX type-2 bone translation/rotation offsets and non-nested type-0 groups whose children are supported vertex or bone morphs. Support bone-only VMD morph tracks without dummy geometry targets.

Retain current vertex/group behavior and legacy asset compatibility. UV, material, flip, impulse and nested-group execution remain separate work with explicit diagnostics. VMD animation and VPD poses remain mandatory in the overall goal; this Issue does not establish overall completion or original-MMD fidelity.

## Context

The [PMX format-author document mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hirakuni45/glfw3_app/master/glfw3_app/docs/PMX_spec.txt) defines bone translation/quaternion offsets, group contribution rates and bone-morph inputs before ordered deformation. It excludes grouping groups. It does not fully settle multiple quaternion contribution behavior or provide controlled original-MMD measurements.

[Core glTF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/glTF/main/specification/2.0/Specification.adoc) represents attribute morph deltas and resolved joint TRS/animation. Therefore retain core representations where sufficient and add one optional runtime-independent `MMD_morphs` contract for missing bone/group control semantics. Version the existing VMD transport as necessary; reuse existing solver, physics, Toon and Outline contracts.

Representation correction: the earlier bounded implementation equates an executable morph with a geometry target. That remains valid for its legacy vertex profile. For the new profile, executable scalar identity must be independent of geometry-target identity: bone offsets affect joint transforms, while core morph targets affect vertex attributes. Preserve this old convention, correction, references and rationale in the implementation record.

Quaternion weighting, accumulation and composition need explicit equations and evidence labels. [Official Three.js quaternion source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mrdoob/three.js/r186/src/math/Quaternion.js) supplies implementation reference, not MMD semantics. Preserve justified existing composition conventions; do not silently reorder append behavior based on ambiguous format wording. Unmeasured choices must remain identified as project policies.

Dependencies/tooling already include Three.js 0.186.1, glTF Transform 4.5.1, mmd-parser 1.1.4, ammojs-typed 1.0.6, Ajv, gltf-validator and Playwright 1.56.1. Extend these paths without an unrelated framework or dependency upgrade.

[PR #46](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/46) reports an earlier complete 108-Node/62-browser pass with two optional skips, followed by 110 Node and four focused browser passes after fixes. The complete browser run predates those fixes. Inspected PR-head and merged CI browser steps remain in progress. Existing test code and reported execution are distinct evidence.

## Pre-merge acceptance

Tests and PR review belong to the Coordinator. All checks below are achievable before merge.

- [ ] Define the optional morph contract, schema, standalone minimal glTF and valid/invalid semantic fixtures. Specify stable model/morph/bone identities, node references, units, defaults, supported families, independent control weights, evaluation order and fallback. Include a bone-morph example requiring no POSITION targets or PMX extras. Preserve older payload semantics and reject inconsistent overlapping metadata.
- [ ] Preserve bone offsets through both PMX parser paths and converter API/CLI in supported BDEF/SDEF/QDEF modes, for GLB and external-buffer glTF. Demonstrate reflection and translation scaling exactly once. Validate bone references, counts, finite values, quaternion policy and numeric/work limits before publishing output. Retain indexed unsupported-family diagnostics; a group with an unsupported child must not execute partially.
- [ ] Specify and implement deterministic direct/group contribution reduction, translation accumulation, quaternion weighting/composition and source ordering. Cover zero, fractional, negative and greater-than-one supported weights, equivalent quaternion signs, noncommuting rotations, duplicate group entries, forward/shared references and zero rates. Preserve independent controls and prevent double application of compiled vertex-group contributions. Existing vertex-only target indices and legacy results remain compatible.
- [ ] Apply bone-morph inputs once from immutable rest plus the selected raw VMD/VPD baseline, before ordered deformation. With physics enabled, evaluate animated contributions at every simulation tick, including initialization, before the existing pre-phase/body/simulation/post-phase pipeline. Do not feed resolved joints back as raw input. Cover IK and append sources affected by morphs, physics coupling and disabled-physics behavior.
- [ ] Extend reusable manual controls, VMD binding and retained playback to use stable scalar identities independent of target count. Bone-only morph motion contributes to duration and playback. Preserve exact-name/byte-map binding, duplicate/ambiguous-name failures and explicit omission reporting. Manual changes pause motion and recompute from the retained raw baseline; VPD apply/reset preserves control weights and recomposes them without inventing VPD morph channels. Define and test physics-history invalidation, stop/reset, resume, seek and looping.
- [ ] Generate resolved core joint animation for every morph-affected joint, including joints without VMD bone tracks, while preserving vertex weight fallback. Extension-aware playback replaces its complete matching fallback once. Validate outputs with gltf-validator plus custom schema/semantic checks. Measure ordinary-loader fallback at keys and fractional probes using existing adaptive or fixed-tick policies, tolerances, seams and budget failures; disclose finite-probe limits.
- [ ] Add attributed synthetic fixtures covering two distinct rig geometries/hierarchies, two motions and both existing VPD poses. Include bone-only controls and mixed groups. Independently authored numerical predictions must distinguish noncommuting composition, duplicate contributions, wrong order and double application. Cover direct conversion/binding, retained GLB/glTF, manual controls, VPD handoffs, failure atomicity, instance isolation, replacement and disposal. Expected values must not be generated by the production morph evaluator.
- [ ] Extend existing GPU/raster and built-Demo tooling to observe the new deformation on Toon/PBR surfaces and Outline, including BDEF and mixed SDEF/QDEF integration. Exercise both rigs/motions through bytes/GLB/glTF and both VPD handoffs; focused advanced-skinning coverage may supplement that matrix. Verify matching rendered revisions, CPU queries, palettes and bounds. Preserve stricter existing suite limits; new integrated cases retain CPU position ≤2e-6 m, GPU position ≤1e-4 m, normal-component error ≤5e-4 and at most 128 pixels differing by more than two byte levels. Retain nonempty intrinsic captures and display evidence.
- [ ] Applied-state GLB/glTF exports validate and reload with the visible pose/weights, original rest and executable morph contract intact. Loading must not apply deformation again. Repeated VPD/VMD/manual application and explicit physics restart must produce documented results without cumulative offsets.
- [ ] Record Coordinator implementation-stage results using the repository workflow: `npm ci`, `npm run build` before generated-asset-dependent checks, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, Chromium installation when needed, `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_CHANNEL=chromium npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links` and `git diff --check`. Preserve relevant existing regression coverage, thresholds and timeouts. Identify tested revisions, failures, skips and unperformed checks; distinguish analytical, backend, alternative-renderer and original-MMD evidence. No independent evaluation rerun or additional AI re-review is required.

Evidence-backed corrections to AI-authored requirements are permitted without human approval or independent AI re-review. Retain the old assumption, corrected requirement, inspected primary source and rationale. Preserve the goal and relevant acceptance; unfinished code or failing tests do not justify weakening requirements.

## Optional validation

Compare the synthetic noncommuting bone-morph probes with version-labelled original MikuMikuDance measurements if a lawful execution environment is available. Record inputs, weights, observation method and differences. Additional attributed representative models are useful. Neither alternative-renderer output nor self-consistency establishes original-MMD equivalence.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed MMD/glTF model, VMD animation and
VPD pose reproduction goal. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
